full_text_en:
**China Music Copyright Association v. NetEase.com, Inc. and Beijing Mobile Communications Co., Ltd. — Dispute over Infringement of the Right of Communication Through Information Network**

**Plaintiff:** China Music Copyright Association. Domicile: Dongsi South Street, Dongcheng District, Beijing.
**Legal Representative:** Wang Liping, Chairman of the Association.

**Defendant:** Guangzhou NetEase Computer System Co., Ltd. (hereinafter "NetEase"). Domicile: Huanshi East Road, Guangzhou City, Guangdong Province.
**Legal Representative:** Ding Lei, Chairman of the Board.

**Defendant:** Beijing Mobile Communications Co., Ltd. (hereinafter "Mobile Communications"). Domicile: Dongzhong Street, Dongcheng District, Beijing.
**Legal Representative:** Sha Yuejia, Chairman of the Board.

The plaintiff, China Music Copyright Association (hereinafter "Music Copyright Association"), filed a lawsuit with the Beijing No. 2 Intermediate People's Court against the defendants, Guangzhou NetEase Computer System Co., Ltd. (hereinafter "NetEase") and Beijing Mobile Communications Co., Ltd. (hereinafter "Mobile Communications"), regarding a dispute over infringement of the right of communication through information network.

The plaintiff alleged: Our Association, entrusted by the composer Su Yue, manages the rights of public performance, broadcasting, recording and distribution, and communication through information network for the musical work "Bloodstained Elegance." On the website www.163.com (hereinafter "163 website") owned by NetEase, NetEase, without authorization, provided the song "Bloodstained Elegance" in its "Ringtone Messaging" service for mobile phone users to download as ringtones. When providing paid information services to mobile phone users, Mobile Communications enabled such users to freely download the said song. The above commercial acts of the two defendants constitute infringement of the copyright of the composer of "Bloodstained Elegance."

The plaintiff's claims were: (1) an order that the two defendants immediately cease using the musical work "Bloodstained Elegance"; (2) a public apology; (3) joint payment of economic damages in the amount of RMB 113,182.5; and (4) compensation for the plaintiff's reasonable expenses incurred in stopping the infringement, totaling RMB 6,300.

The defendant NetEase argued: The evidence provided by the plaintiff cannot prove that Su Yue is the copyright owner of the song "Bloodstained Elegance." Since Mobile Communications has already collected certain service fees and asymmetric communication fees, the number of clicks on the song as displayed on the 163 website cannot be used as the basis for our company's revenue. The plaintiff's claim that our company should compensate damages at five times its profit has no legal basis.

The defendant Mobile Communications argued: As a telecommunications operator, our company only acts as a transmission conduit in mobile communication services and has no fault in the infringement. The plaintiff's request that our company bear infringement liability has no legal basis.

The Beijing No. 2 Intermediate People's Court found upon trial:

The composer of "Bloodstained Elegance" is Su Yue. On January 18, 1994, Su Yue entered into a music copyright contract with the plaintiff Music Copyright Association, entrusting the Association with the management of the rights of public performance, broadcasting, and recording and distribution of the musical work. On October 9, 2001, Su Yue entered into a supplementary contract with the Music Copyright Association, also authorizing the Association to manage the rights relating to uploading, downloading, and transmission of the musical work on the Internet.

On the 163 website operated by the defendant NetEase, there is a "NetEase SMS Center" recommendation service. Among its columns, the "Ringtone Messaging" section contains numerous musical works that users can select for download as ringtones for mobile phones. When NetEase included "Bloodstained Elegance" in the folk song category of this column, it did not obtain permission from Su Yue or the Music Copyright Association and did not pay any remuneration.

The above service provided by NetEase was conducted through specialized equipment and technical conditions provided by the mobile communications department. When mobile phone users select this service on the 163 website, they first log onto the 163 website via the telecommunications department's Internet, select the desired song on the relevant webpage, whereupon NetEase's server compiles the song into binary code, sends it via the Internet to the mobile SMS platform of the mobile communications department, which then sends it to the mobile phone user. Mobile phone users nationwide must go through their local mobile communications departments to complete the above download process. On the page of the 163 website, there is a public statistical display of the number of clicks for each musical work, which represents the number of times mobile phone users nationwide have listened to or downloaded the musical work through the mobile communications department.

On November 21, 2001, NetEase and Mobile Communications entered into a cooperation agreement. The parties agreed: Mobile Communications would collect the fees for user downloads of songs on behalf of NetEase; NetEase would pay Mobile Communications a 15% service fee; the basis for settlement would be the full amount of information fees receivable for the month as recorded in the billing system of Mobile Communications. In addition, when providing transmission services for musical information to NetEase, Mobile Communications would charge NetEase an asymmetric communication fee of RMB 0.05 per message.

Under the existing technical conditions, when providing transmission services for musical information, Mobile Communications is unable to identify, record, or edit the transmitted musical information, nor can it individually remove or filter any specific musical information. During the process of receiving and transmitting information through automated equipment, human control is not possible.

The fee charged by NetEase to mobile phone users for downloading each song was: RMB 1 for ordinary quality ringtones and RMB 2 for high-fidelity quality ringtones. As of November 28, 2001, the number of clicks displayed on the 163 website for the song "Bloodstained Elegance" was 15,091.

The above facts are confirmed by the following evidence: the music copyright contract and supplementary agreement between the Music Copyright Association and Su Yue; the work registration form; the notarized certificate; webpage materials; the Mobile Dream Network customer manual and network access fee receipt; the "Explanation Concerning Issues Related to the Mobile Dream Network SMS Business Cooperation between Beijing Mobile Communications Co., Ltd. and Guangzhou NetEase Computer System Co., Ltd." provided by Mobile Communications; and the statements of all parties.

The Beijing No. 2 Intermediate People's Court held:

Based on the evidence submitted by the parties, it should be determined that Su Yue is the composer of the song "Bloodstained Elegance." The copyright entrustment management contract between Su Yue and the Music Copyright Association is legally valid, and the relevant registration procedures completed by the parties are also genuine and effective. Although NetEase raised questions regarding the registration procedures between Su Yue and the Music Copyright Association, it failed to provide evidence to support its claims; therefore, those objections are not accepted. The Music Copyright Association, based on Su Yue's authorization and relevant legal provisions, filed this lawsuit as the plaintiff, and its standing as a litigant should be confirmed.

Pursuant to Article 10, paragraph 1, item (12) of the Copyright Law of the People's Republic of China (hereinafter "Copyright Law"), a copyright owner enjoys the right of communication through information network, i.e., the right to provide works to the public through the Internet or other wired or wireless information transmission networks. Acts of making another person's work available online for public use without permission constitute infringement of the copyright owner's right of communication through information network. NetEase, without permission, directly included the musical work "Bloodstained Elegance" in a column on the 163 website for public display, and provided it for download to mobile phone users on a fee-paying basis. This act constitutes infringement of the copyright owner's right of communication through information network, and NetEase shall bear civil liability to cease the infringement and compensate for losses. However, the Music Copyright Association failed to prove that NetEase's acts infringed upon the personal rights of the copyright owner Su Yue or caused adverse effects to Su Yue personally or to the work. Accordingly, the Music Copyright Association's claim for an order requiring NetEase to make a public apology to Su Yue and the Music Copyright Association is not supported. As for the issue of damages for NetEase's infringement, since the amount of damages claimed by the Music Copyright Association has no legal basis, it shall be determined at the court's discretion based on factors such as the manner in which NetEase used the work at issue and its actual profit gained.

For the plaintiff Music Copyright Association to request that Mobile Communications bear infringement liability, it must prove that Mobile Communications disseminated the infringing work on the network in the form of direct publication, or that it had a duty to review the received and transmitted information but neglected to do so, or that, after being notified by the rights holder of the transmission of infringing information, it could have stopped the transmission of such information but failed to do so. In this case, the network information transmission service provided by Mobile Communications to NetEase was technical and passive in nature; specifically, it provided basic technical connection services for receiving information sent by NetEase and sending it to mobile phone users, enabling two-way communication from mobile phones to the Internet or from the Internet to mobile phones. In providing this network information connection service, the information received by Mobile Communications was published by NetEase. During the process of receiving and sending information, the transmitted information remained in binary code at all times. Mobile Communications could not select the content of the transmitted information, nor could it individually delete any particular piece of information. Moreover, when providing transmission services to mobile communication customers and network companies, Mobile Communications did not bear the duty to review the specific content of the transmitted information and, in practice, was unable to conduct such review. Therefore, subjectively, there was no legal fault on the part of Mobile Communications regarding the occurrence of the infringement; requiring it to bear joint infringement liability lacks legal basis. Considering the actual circumstances of this case, ordering the provider of the infringing information, NetEase, to cease publishing the infringing information is sufficient to stop the continuation of the infringement. Further ordering Mobile Communications, which merely provided basic technical services, to bear joint infringement liability would be detrimental to the public interest and to the application and development of network technology. The fact that Mobile Communications charges fees for providing basic equipment services cannot be used as a reason to require it to bear infringement liability. Therefore, Mobile Communications' acts do not constitute infringement of the copyright in the song "Bloodstained Elegance."

In summary, pursuant to Article 10, paragraph 1, item (12) and Article 47, paragraph 1, item (1) of the Copyright Law, the Beijing No. 2 Intermediate People's Court rendered the following judgment on September 20, 2002:

1. Guangzhou NetEase Computer System Co., Ltd. shall immediately cease disseminating the song "Bloodstained Elegance" to the public on the Internet.
2. Guangzhou NetEase Computer System Co., Ltd. shall pay damages in the amount of RMB 10,000 and notarization fees in the amount of RMB 1,300 to the China Music Copyright Association within ten days after this judgment takes effect.
3. The other claims of the China Music Copyright Association are dismissed.

Court acceptance fee: RMB 3,900, of which RMB 1,000 shall be borne by the China Music Copyright Association and RMB 2,900 by Guangzhou NetEase Computer System Co., Ltd.

After the judgment was pronounced, neither party appealed, and the judgment became legally effective.
